title: Libretto
rule: An opera: the lines set as sung parts under ruled staves, with stage directions.
declares: keeps E0-E5, the four lines and the outcome
made: four stage pictures printed as HANDMADE stencils in flat dyes (wash, ochre, verdigris, indigo, madder, skin, umber), the page-08 stencil method: one cut stencil per colour from the b1m2 cut model, paper ties, fixed misregistration, mottled dye pooling at the edges, on the LoC 1934 sheet
a stencilled proscenium in every picture: madder curtains and valance with cut fold slits, umber apron and boards, ochre footlights
the ANRC 1922 key cutout used as the ochre key stencil in picture 4
title 'THE SERVICE KEY' stencilled in madder with a bridge (tie) cut across every letter

ruled five-line staves (pen line), pen treble clefs and 4/4, notes stencilled in umber (filled and open heads, stems, flags, ledger lines), our own melodies; the canon lines underlaid syllable by syllable

role names AGENT / STRANGER / Orch. at the staves; stage directions in parentheses, the pen hand sheared to an italic, in a madder rubric; numbers and tempo marks (No. 1 Prelude, No. 2 Recitative, No. 3 Duettino, No. 4 Aria)

picture 2 re-staged: the agent stands right of the ticket window and faces it (left), the wall clock hangs high behind him on the right, clear of his head; every agent stencil recoloured to the canon marks: indigo waistcoat over white shirtsleeves and shirt front (sleeve and shirt shapes cut out of every dye stencil, an umber cut-edge line and garter band printed round them)

events.E0: No. 1 Prelude: direction (memo on the desk, he rises and sets off); picture 1 desk, memo slip, agent setting off; orchestra staff 'tick tock'
events.E1: No. 2 Recitative: direction (stranger at the ticket window stops him); STRANGER sings the question
events.E2: No. 3 Duettino: direction (he looks up at the clock: ten past four); picture 3 clock at 4:10; AGENT sings the answer
events.E3: No. 3: STRANGER sings 'Much obliged!'; direction (She leaves the window.)
events.E4: No. 4 Aria: direction (he opens the cupboard; the key on its hook, tagged SERVICE); picture 4
events.E5: No. 4: AGENT sings the forgetting line, pencil at chin; closing direction: key stays on its hook, SERVICE door stays closed, slow curtain

lines.question: Pardon me — have you the right time?
lines.answer: Ten past four, by the clock.
lines.forgetting: Well, here I am... and what for?

substitutions: none: the four lines verbatim as sung text (syllables hyphenated only)
beat: the score is filled number by number as it is sung (empty staves, then prelude, question, answer, thanks, aria), then the stencilled curtain closes over the last picture
beat_frames: b06: + No. 4 AGENT: the aria (the finished page)
b07: the curtain half closed over picture 4

self_check.check: A reader finds staves, role names and stage directions (maker's judgement from the full-size page: five ruled staves with clefs and notes, role names at each staff, parenthesised italic directions in red; blind reading pending)
self_check.evidence: measured (size, bytes) and perceptually judged (from frames) by the maker

picture2_clock_vs_head.agent_faces: left, toward the TICKET OFFICE window

self_check.canon_marks: waistcoat (indigo) over white shirtsleeves in all four pictures

weaknesses: the stranger's figure behind the window glass is small and partly crossed by the glazing bars
eighth-note flags are crude stencil curls; the music is notation-shaped rather than engraved
in picture 4 his forearm is hidden behind the open cupboard leaf; only the pencil at his chin shows
repairs: repair 2026-11-17 (batch 3): picture 2 clock moved off the agent's head (81 px clear, masks disjoint), agent faces the window; waistcoat and shirtsleeves
